audits.design:
THE ROOT CAUSE IS ONE LOSSY ADAPTER, NOT TEN SCATTERED CALLS.

`Kernel::wait_child_matching` (operations.rs:3251) already returns `WaitOutcome::Exited(Zombie)`, and `Zombie` (objects.rs:4146) already carries `key`, `parent`, `process_group`, `session`, `status`, `euid`, `rusage`, `children_rusage`. Then `hvpatch::ProcessContext::wait_child_*` (hvpatch/mod.rs:759, 819, 877) narrows all of that to `ChildExit { pid: TaskId, status: i32 }` (hvpatch/mod.rs:291). Dispatch is handed two integers, so when it needs si_uid it reaches for `libc::getuid()` and when it needs rusage it invents zeros. Every defect above is downstream of that narrowing. The fix is to stop narrowing, not to patch call sites.

1. DELETE `ChildExit`. Per AGENTS.md ("no backward compatibility, replace it and delete the old one"), make the hvpatch adapter return the kernel's own type:

     pub(crate) enum WaitResult {
         Reaped(ReapedChild),      // terminal, zombie consumed or observed
         JobControl(JobControlEvent),
         StillRunning,
         NoChild,
         NoSuchProcessGroup,       // NEW — see 3
     }

     pub(crate) struct ReapedChild {
         pid: TaskId,
         status: LinuxWaitStatus,  // typed, not i32
         uid: NsUid,               // child's REAL uid at exit
         rusage: TaskRusage,       // child's own CPU
     }

   `ReapedChild` is minted only by the kernel from a `Zombie`; it has no public constructor from parts. That makes `libc::getuid()` and `LinuxRusage::zeroed()` unwritable at proc.rs:3082 and 3500 — the fields are simply there.

2. TYPE THE WAIT STATUS AND KILL THE BARE `from_wait_encoding`. `LinuxWaitStatus(i32)` (objects.rs:4125) has a general `from_wait_encoding(raw: i32)` — precisely the "no general from_raw" rule AGENTS.md states for polarity/direction-carrying domains, and this one carries three mutually-colliding encodings (`(sig<<8)|0x7f` stop, `0xffff` continue, `(code<<8)` exit, `sig|0x80` dumped). `hvpatch_waitid_exit_fields` (proc.rs:4883) exists only because the encoding was flattened and has to be re-parsed, with a comment warning that the collision already bit once. Replace with named semantic constructors —
     LinuxWaitStatus::exited(ExitCode)
     LinuxWaitStatus::killed(Signal, CoreDumped)
     LinuxWaitStatus::stopped(Signal)
     LinuxWaitStatus::continued()
   — and accessors `fn classify(self) -> WaitStatusKind`. `run_result.rs:118 wait_status_encoding` becomes the single `.raw()` escape at the guest-memory boundary. The three literal `(signal.raw() << 8) | 0x7f` / `0xffff` sites in hvpatch/mod.rs (789, 795, 843, 849, 903, 909) collapse into constructor calls.

3. ADD PROCESS-GROUP EXISTENCE TO THE WAIT QUERY. `wait_child_matching` gains, for the `process_group: Some(group)` case, a pre-check answered from `state.process_groups` — but the check must be "group record exists OR any zombie carries `zombie.process_group == group`". That precision is load-bearing: `remove_group_member` (operations.rs:3020) destroys the group record when its last LIVE member exits, so a naive existence probe would turn a legitimate reap of the group's last zombie into ESRCH. Absent → `WaitOutcome::NoSuchProcessGroup` → `LINUX_ESRCH` at proc.rs:3480 and at the `waitid` P_PGID arm (proc.rs:3025). This replaces the host `kill(pgid, 0)` probe at proc.rs:3872 outright.

4. PUT `exit_signal` IN THE GRAPH. Add `exit_signal: Option<Signal>` to `Task` and `Zombie` (`None` == "does not signal on exit", i.e. a __WCLONE-eligible child; `Some(SIGCHLD)` == ordinary fork). Set it from `ClonePlan` at `reserve_fork` — the plan already carries `fork_parent` for CLONE_PARENT (kernel/clone_plan.rs:90), so this is the same seam. Then `WaitJobControl` grows a companion `WaitChildClass { SigchldOnly, CloneOnly, All }` derived from `__WALL`/`__WCLONE` in `LinuxWaitOptions`, and `wait_child_matching`'s three predicates (zombie scan, state-change scan, live-child scan) each add the class filter. This also lets `KernelState::child_exit_signal` (vcpu_loop/mod.rs:1148) be deleted — the notifier reads the signal from the zombie it just published instead of from a runtime-side copy, which is the same "graph is the authority" move.

5. AUTO-REAP. `prepare_task_exit_key_for_adopter` consults the PARENT task's SIGCHLD disposition (available via `KernelTaskSignalSnapshot`, already used by `child_exit_signal_snapshot_needs_pump`, dispatch/signal.rs:377). If the parent has SIGCHLD == SIG_IGN or SA_NOCLDWAIT, publish no `ZombieRecord` at all — charge `total_charge_to_reaper()` to the parent's children ledger immediately and release the `TaskClaim`. That is Linux's rule and it is the only thing that bounds pid growth for the SIG_IGN case. Separately, give the run-root adopter an implicit-reap policy so an orphan reparented to a root that never waits does not pin a `TaskClaim` forever (the "~1,600 accumulated guest pids" shape in the handoff).

6. TARGETED CHILD-EXIT WAKE. `HvpatchRuntimeDirectory::notify_child_exit` (vcpu_loop/mod.rs:717) already resolves the exact parent `TaskKey`. Give `Task` a per-task child-wait wait queue (a `WaitQueue` beside `job_control_changed`, which is already a per-task `Condvar` — copy that shape rather than inventing a second one) and have the exit path post to THAT instead of `HvpatchTaskWaker::wake_task`'s four-way carrier-wide broadcast. This satisfies the futex-requeue doc's stated bar ("each caller has to be shown to know its target") for one of its ~30 broadcast callers. `WaitOnHvpatchChild`'s 10 ms poll (vcpu_loop/mod.rs:3389) then becomes a pure backstop rather than the wake's real latency floor.

7. MAKE THE LANE SPLIT A TYPE, NOT AN `if`. Every host wait in proc.rs is correct today only because `if let Some(process) = this.hvpatch_process()` returns first (proc.rs:2999 for waitid, 3444 for wait4). That guard is re-derived per handler and nothing enforces it. Land the `Authority { Guest, Host, Hybrid }` column that docs/host-facility-boundary.md already proposes for `Syscall`, and extend `.semgrep/typed-domains.yml` (run by `just lint-domains` inside `just ci`) so a `Guest`-authority row's dispatch path may not name `libc::wait4`, `libc::waitid`, `libc::waitpid`, `libc::getuid`, `libc::getpgrp`, `libc::kill` or `std::process::id`. `process`/`ipc`/`signal`/`sched` = 133 rows, 39% of the aarch64 table. Use the monotonic-baseline form the identity-and-scope doc specifies (fail on any finding not in the baseline AND on a baseline entry that stops matching) so the native/VMM sites here stay allowed and the file can only shrink.

WHAT THE HOST STILL LEGITIMATELY OWNS HERE, AND WHY: every `libc::wait4`/`libc::waitid` outside the two HVPatch branches reaps a REAL host process and must stay. Three distinct populations justify them. (a) The DSR/native lanes (`PtraceTransport::VirtualNative`) genuinely fork host processes per guest process — sites 545, 3182, 3290, 3617, 3681. (b) The legacy VMM lanes likewise — 3251, 3355, 3706, 3749. (c) Carrick's own infrastructure children under ANY lane: `file_authority/ipc.rs:102` reaps its double-fork launcher with a targeted `waitpid(launcher, ..., 0)` — that is exactly right and must never be routed through the graph, and it runs at startup "before guest threads exist" so no guest wait can race it. The teardown `posix_spawn("/bin/rm", ...)` at fs_backend.rs:1890 is deliberately unreaped and documented as such. This is the same distinction docs/host-facility-boundary.md draws for sysv/mqueue: the segments live in real files, so their open/pread/pwrite are backing-store I/O and stay. Here, the host processes are real host processes, so the waits that name them stay — what must go is any wait that names a GUEST task.
audits.risk:
WHAT CAN HANG.

1. Auto-reap (item 5) is the dangerous one. Removing the `ZombieRecord` means `wait_child_matching` finds no zombie and no live child, so it returns `NoChild` → ECHILD. Linux's rule for SIG_IGN is subtler: a blocking `wait()` must BLOCK until all children have exited and only THEN return ECHILD, not return ECHILD immediately while children are still running. Get that backwards and any SIG_IGN parent's `wait()` loop spins or exits early. The live-child scan at operations.rs:3339 already distinguishes StillRunning from NoChild, so the ordering is expressible — but it must be tested with a live child present, not only after all children are gone.

2. The targeted wake (item 6) trades a thundering herd for a lost-wake hang. The futex-requeue doc's closing note is explicit: "a missed wake is a hang", which is why that broadcast was left in place after the durability fix. The safe sequencing is to add the per-task child-wait queue and post to it IN ADDITION to the existing broadcast, prove the 10 ms `WaitOnHvpatchChild` backstop never fires in a fork-storm run (instrument via `trace_hvpatch_wait_begin/end`, vcpu_loop/mod.rs:3358-3369, whose TimedOut-vs-Ready arms already distinguish the two), and only then remove the broadcast. Never both at once — that is the exact mistake the requeue campaign made and reverted (05e83fee0).

3. `LinuxWaitStatus` retyping (item 2) touches ~40 construction sites, most in tests. `from_wait_encoding(0)` appears everywhere as "exit 0"; a mechanical rewrite to `LinuxWaitStatus::exited(ExitCode::SUCCESS)` should go through scripts/migrate/rewrite.py as a count-asserted spec, not hand edits.

4. The ESRCH-vs-ECHILD change (item 3) can turn a working reap into ESRCH if the zombie fallback is omitted — see the design note about `remove_group_member` destroying the group record while a zombie member survives. Any regression shows up as a shell losing a background job.

5. Item 4 (`exit_signal` filtering) changes what a DEFAULT `wait4(-1)` reaps: today it reaps everything, after the change it reaps only SIGCHLD children. If any carrick-internal clone path forgets to set `Some(SIGCHLD)`, that child becomes unreapable by an ordinary wait and its parent hangs forever. Default the field to `Some(SIGCHLD)` and make the non-SIGCHLD case the explicit one.

HOW A REVIEWER CATCHES ALL OF IT: every item is guest-observable from a two-process reducer, so the review question is simply "which probe went red first, and does it MATCH the Docker oracle after". Do not accept a diff without a named red-first receipt — AGENTS.md's rule that "a probe that passes immediately proves nothing" is exactly load-bearing here, because `waitidspec` and `waitpgid` both currently pass while the defects they nominally cover are live. Concretely: `waitidspec` passes today and asserts nothing about si_uid; `waitpgid` passes today only because `i32::MIN` short-circuits before the kernel is asked. A reviewer should demand the ADDED assertions be shown failing against the unmodified signed binary. Note also that these are HVPatch-lane changes, so per AGENTS.md the integration gate must additionally smoke the still-shipped default/native lane — the host wait4/waitid sites listed as legitimate must keep working, and items 1/3/4/5 all touch code the native lane shares.
audits.test_shape:
RED-FIRST REDUCER: one new probe, `conformance-probes/src/bin/waitidentity.rs`, plus two additive assertions to existing probes. Every phase runs TWO live guest processes at once, which is the property docs/identity-and-scope-domains.md identifies as the only way this class becomes visible — a single guest process makes the carrier pid, the root task id and `getuid()` coincide, so the smoke lane structurally cannot see any of it.

`waitidentity` — line-exact, no timing assertions, all booleans:

  Phase A (si_uid; catches proc.rs:3082). Parent forks child X (exits 7) and child Y (exits 9) so TWO guest processes are live simultaneously. Reap X with `waitid(P_PID, X, &si, WEXITED)`. Assert `si_uid_is_zero = si.si_uid == 0` and `si_pid_is_child = si.si_pid == X`. On carrick today si_uid is the Mac uid (501); under Docker it is 0. RED immediately, for the exact right reason, with Y still alive so the carrier holds two tasks.

  Phase B (wait4 rusage; catches proc.rs:3499). Child burns ~300 ms of CPU in a spin loop while a SIBLING child sleeps — again two live guest processes. Reap the burner with `wait4(pid, &st, 0, &ru)`. Assert `wait4_rusage_nonzero = ru.ru_utime.tv_sec + ru.ru_utime.tv_usec > 0` and `wait4_rusage_below_wall = ...` so the case is machine-speed independent. This deliberately mirrors `timeschildren.rs`, which proved the SAME data path for `times()`/`getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN)` on 2026-08-13 and left wait4's own out-param untested — reuse its ordering-and-sign-only style rather than inventing a second one.

  Phase C (pgid ESRCH; catches proc.rs:3480). With a live child in the caller's own group, call `waitpid(-999999, &st, WNOHANG)` for a representable-but-nonexistent pgid. Assert `waitpid_absent_pgid_esrch = rc == -1 && errno == ESRCH`. Then, in the same phase, `setpgid` a second child into its own new group, let it exit WITHOUT reaping it, and assert `waitpid_zombie_only_group_reaps = waitpid(-newpgid, &st, 0) == thatchild` — this is the regression guard for the `remove_group_member` subtlety, and it is the assertion most likely to catch a wrong fix.

  Phase D (__WCLONE/__WALL; catches the missing Task::exit_signal). Create child C1 with `clone(..., SIGCHLD)` and C2 with `clone(..., SIGUSR1)`, both live. Assert `wclone_skips_sigchld_child = waitpid(-1, &st, __WCLONE|WNOHANG)` never returns C1, and `default_skips_clone_child = waitpid(-1, &st, WNOHANG)` never returns C2. Today both return whichever exited first.

  Phase E (SIG_IGN auto-reap; catches the missing SA_NOCLDWAIT/SIG_IGN rule). `signal(SIGCHLD, SIG_IGN)`, fork two children, let both exit, then assert `sigign_wait_is_echild = wait(NULL) == -1 && errno == ECHILD`. Then the ordering guard that protects against the hang in risk item 1: with SIG_IGN set and one child still SLEEPING, assert a `waitpid(-1, &st, WNOHANG)` returns 0 (not ECHILD) — i.e. the blocking form would have blocked.

ADDITIVE ASSERTIONS to existing probes (cheap, and they close the gate holes that let these ship):
  - `waitidspec.rs`: add `si_uid` and `si_pid` assertions to case 1 and case 2. Both are pure additions to existing `report!` blocks.
  - `waitpgid.rs`: add the representable-nonexistent-pgid case beside the existing `i32::MIN` one, so the probe stops passing for the wrong reason.

PROVING RED FIRST, per AGENTS.md: write the probe, build signed via `just build`, run `cargo test -p carrick-cli --test conformance conformance_probes` FROM THE REPO ROOT (from any other cwd it SKIPs every lane and reports ok in 0.04s — a green that gated nothing), and confirm a DIFF against the Docker oracle for each named assertion. Then land the kernel-graph changes and confirm MATCH. Grep all gate logs with `grep -a`; they carry binary bytes. Run the carrick and Docker phases serially — never concurrently.

WHAT BREAKS FOR --net=host USERS
(a) Steady state: nothing. The host-mirror seed runs the same ranked mapping `support.rs:955` runs today, so rtnetlink and /proc/net emit byte-identical output.
(b) `/sys/class/net` stops listing `en0`, `awdl0`, `utun*`, `bridge0`, `llw0`, `anpi0`, `ap1`, `gif0`, `stf0` and starts listing `lo` + `eth0`. That is the fix, not a regression: today `/sys/class/net/eth0/address` is ENOENT while the rtnetlink dump advertises eth0 with a MAC.
(c) THE ONE REAL COST: the view becomes a snapshot. A `--net=host` daemon that re-reads its addresses after the Mac joins a different Wi-Fi network or raises a VPN `utun` sees the change today on its next `getifaddrs()`. Docker `--net=host` on Linux watches the real host netns and does see live changes, so a frozen snapshot is a fidelity LOSS. This is why the `PF_ROUTE` watcher is part of the change and not a follow-up. A `PF_ROUTE` socket is a plain fd (fork-safe, no CoreFoundation, unlike the SCDynamicStore route that would be the obvious macOS answer and would reintroduce the ObjC-fork abort commit eb7dede87 just removed).
(d) Multiple host uplinks: today exactly one becomes eth0 and the rest vanish. The model can expose `eth0..ethN`, which is closer to Docker `--net=host` but changes ifindexes for anything that assumed 2 — safe only because `linux_if_nametoindex` is deleted in the same change.
(e) `SIOCGIFNETMASK` stops returning /32 and `SIOCGIFMTU` stops returning 1500 for `lo`. Strictly closer to Linux; a guest that keyed on the old values changes behaviour.

audits.risk:
HANG RISK, the one that matters. The `PF_ROUTE` watcher must never be something a guest syscall waits on. If the view is behind a `Mutex` and the watcher holds it across its blocking `read()`, every guest `getifaddrs`/`/proc/net` read wedges behind a socket that may not deliver an event for hours — a carrier at 0% CPU, exactly the shape docs/identity-and-scope-domains.md §5 describes. Design it as `ArcSwap<NetNsView>` (RCU): the read path is a load with no lock, the watcher only ever publishes. A reviewer catches a violation by grepping for any lock acquired on the read path of `NetNs::view`, and by taking a core with `carrick debug lldb-run` on the CARRIER (not the orchestrator parent) and confirming no thread is parked in `NetNs`.

FORK RISK. `PF_ROUTE` is a plain fd and is fork-safe; the watcher THREAD is not. On the lanes that still host-fork for `execve`, a child inherits a dead watcher's bookkeeping. Start the watcher only in the VM carrier and register it with the existing fork guard machinery (`network::NetworkForkGuard`, network/mod.rs) rather than inventing a second mechanism. This is also the trap commit eb7dede87 just paid for: reaching for SCDynamicStore/SCNetworkReachability instead of `PF_ROUTE` would reintroduce the `+[NSNumber initialize]` fork abort verbatim.

REGRESSION RISK, netlink encoding. Merging `build_netlink_reply` into `build_netlink_reply_for_snapshot` makes host mode start emitting IFA_FLAGS and IFA_CACHEINFO and stop emitting IFA_LOCAL/IFA_LABEL on IPv6 rows. glibc's `__check_pf` and `getifaddrs` both walk those attributes to build address-selection state, so a mistake here shows up as AI_ADDRCONFIG silently discarding every IPv4 DNS answer — the exact failure `linux_guest_interfaces`' portable-fallback comment records from the FreeBSD lane. audits.risk:
HANG / LOCK INVERSION — the one that can wedge a carrier. `nofile_limit()` (fs/fd_helpers.rs:56) runs inside fd allocation, which already holds the file-table lock; `fsize_soft_limit()` (fs.rs:6809) runs on every regular-file write. Making the rlimit read take a `Mutex` on `Task` puts a new lock under the two busiest locks in the runtime, and `replace_rlimit` is called from prlimit64 while the dispatcher may hold others — an inversion of exactly the class docs/identity-and-scope-domains.md §5 records as having already wedged a carrier at 0% CPU once. The mitigation is structural: reads go through `ArcSwap::load` (no lock at all), and `rlimit_write: Mutex<()>` is acquired in exactly one function which calls into no other subsystem. A reviewer verifies with `rg 'rlimit_write' crates/carrick-runtime` returning exactly two hits (the field and its single acquisition) and by reading `replace_rlimit`'s body for any call out.

PRIVILEGE REGRESSION — the highest-severity way to get this wrong. Today prlimit64 does no target-ownership check, which is invisible because the write lands on self. Fixing target resolution WITHOUT adding the EPERM gate converts a harmless no-op into any-guest-process-can-rewrite-any-other's limits, including a root-owned peer's. A reviewer catches it by requiring the ownership probe (below) red-then-green in the SAME commit as the resolution change, and by checking that the target credentials come from `RlimitTarget::Live { credentials }` and not from `cred_snapshot()`.

SILENT NO-OP — the failure that leaves the probe green and the bug live. If the no-`cx` readers fall back to `RlimitSet::carrick_defaults()` when `with_active_context()` returns None, the fd ceiling silently reverts to 1 Mi outside a dispatch scope and every assertion still passes. Reviewer check: `rg 'with_active_context' crates/carrick-runtime/src/dispatch` and confirm each rlimit read follows `cred_snapshot`'s abort-in-release shape (creds.rs:270-274), not `unwrap_or`.

Two paths mint a child Task (`ForkReservation::prepare`, operations.rs:536; the host-fork adapter, dispatch/mod.rs:3413) and they have drifted before, which is why `inherit_fork_attributes_from` exists as one named call. If `inherit_rlimits_from` is open-coded in one of them, single-process runs and every existing rlimit probe still pass. CONFORMANCE CHURN FROM COLLAPSING THE CONTRADICTIONS. Four surfaces currently disagree and pinning them to one authority CHANGES guest-visible numbers: `/proc/self/limits` gains real values (today it is frozen at CORE soft 0, MEMLOCK 65536, SIGPENDING 63880, NPROC unlimited); the `sigq_denominator_matches_limits_max_pending_signals` unit test (vfs/proc.rs:4745) asserts the frozen 63880 and will fail by construction; `/proc/sys/kernel/threads-max` changes from a machine-dependent macOS number to a stable one. Re-bless against the Docker oracle, never against carrick's prior output, and run the carrick and Docker phases serially per AGENTS.md.

MEASUREMENT HAZARD. Do not read any perf delta from a run taken while the current conformance gate is live; and per AGENTS.md a measurement binary must be REBUILT after every merge it claims to cover. The fd-allocation path is hot enough that an `ArcSwap` load versus the current `self.proc.lock()` is worth an ABBA on the fs-walk fixture, but that is a follow-up, not a gate on correctness.

SCOPE HONESTY. The RLIMIT_CPU sites (time.rs:1025/1130/1134) stay broken after this change and get slightly worse in the multi-process case. The commit body must name them as deliberately out of scope with the follow-up, rather than letting "rlimits moved to the kernel graph" read as "rlimits are correct".

audits.risk:
WHAT CAN HANG

1. Job control is the classic hang generator, and step 2 turns it on for the first time. Today `tcsetpgrp` returns EPERM and nothing ever stops; once TIOCSPGRP actually installs a foreground group, a guest process reading from the tty while in a BACKGROUND group must SIGTTIN-stop — and if the orphaned-process-group rule (`setpgid(2)`/`termios(3)`: a read/write from an orphaned pgrp gets EIO, not a stop; an orphaned pgrp with a stopped member gets SIGHUP+SIGCONT) is not implemented in the same change, the group stops with nobody able to continue it and the guest wedges at 0% CPU forever. LTP's `TST_PROCESS_STATE_WAIT` polls `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 3 with NO timeout, so this manifests as a suite sitting on its 300 s budget and being misread as a "490x perf regression" rather than a hang — read the timeout budget before reading the ratio.

2. Lock inversion. `Kernel::set_process_group` (`kernel/operations.rs:2399`) takes `ids().claim_process_group()` and then `registry().state.write()`; `create_session_reserved` takes `state.read()` for the reservation, drops it, allocates claims, then takes `state.write()` and re-validates. Adding a Session-owned controlling terminal means an fd/open-file-description lock enters that window from the `TIOCSPGRP` side while the signal-delivery side already goes registry→signal-queue. AGENTS.md records that a page-table/host-alias order inversion wedged a carrier at 0% CPU once and a re-entrant topology lock turned an intended ENOMEM into an unkillable hang. Mint the tty reference OUTSIDE the registry write (resolve fd → `TtyId` first, then enter), and prefer a token only the outer acquisition can produce over documented discipline.

3. Deleting the host fallbacks (steps 3/4/6) converts "plausible wrong answer" into ESRCH/ENOENT anywhere `hvpatch_process()` is transiently None. `initialize_root_process` binds the root before first guest entry (`hvpatch/mod.rs:1081`) and the fork path binds the child before it is started (`quiesce.rs:1924`), so the window should be empty — but exec (`hvpatch/mod.rs:1618/1635`) re-binds, and a syscall serviced mid-exec with no bound process would now get ESRCH where it previously got a host answer. Verify by making `hvpatch_process()` return `ProcessContext` rather than `Option<ProcessContext>` and letting the compiler enumerate the real gaps, instead of leaving `Option` and reasoning about it.

WHAT CAN REGRESS QUIETLY

4. `NsPid::names_self()` currently returns TRUE for pid 1 from every process. Tightening it to `self.0 == caller_task_pid()` will make some currently-passing cases FAIL — because they were passing by accident on the init process, where caller==1 makes both readings agree. Expect movement in `capget*`, `capset*`, `setpriority*`, `tkill01`, `sched_*`. Every such flip must be checked against Docker before being called a regression: the single-process smoke lane cannot distinguish the two readings at all, which is precisely why this class survived.

5. `readlink("/proc/self")` changing from "1" to the caller's real pid will move any test that has been comparing against 1. That is the fix landing, not a break, but it will look like a diff.

6. Attribution noise. A conformance gate is running on this machine right now; sibling load makes LTP cases fail identically and en masse and the harness self-classifies starved timeouts as `[starved]` rather than `[blocked]`. Any measurement of this change must be taken against a REBUILT unmodified base revision (not `git stash` — the stash is repo-global across worktrees; commit on a branch and `git checkout` the base), sampled at least twice per point, and each suite invoked the way the harness invokes it (`/bin/sh -c`, `--max-traps` disabled).

- The one-line consistency assertion the whole subsystem reduces to: for every live guest process, `getpgid(0)` must equal `/proc/self/stat` field 5 and `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 5 read by a SIBLING, and `getsid(0)` must equal field 6 read by that sibling. Structure: parent forks a child; the child parks on a pipe read so it stays LIVE while the parent inspects it, and the parent writes to the pipe only after every cross-process assertion is taken. audits.design:
GOAL: exactly one way to deliver a Linux signal, and it takes a kernel-graph destination plus an origin that carries the sender's guest identity. No host pid, no carrier-global slot, no second transport.

1. ONE ENTRY POINT, replacing bootstrap_signal_send_as / SignalTarget / the xsig ring / raise_self / raise_for_self.

   // kernel/operations.rs
   pub enum SignalDestination {
       Process(TaskId),                 // kill(pid>0), pidfd, F_OWNER_PID, mq registrant
       Thread(Option<TaskId>, LinuxTid),// tgkill(tgid,tid) / tkill(tid) / F_OWNER_TID
       ProcessGroup(ProcessGroupId),    // kill(-pgid), F_OWNER_PGRP
       CallerGroup,                     // kill(0)
       Broadcast,                       // kill(-1)
       Exact(TaskKey),                  // pidfd / anything already generation-bound
   }
   pub enum SignalOrigin {
       Kill        { sender: TaskKey, ruid: NsUid },                       // SI_USER
       Tkill       { sender: TaskKey, ruid: NsUid },                       // SI_TKILL
       Queued      { sender: TaskKey, ruid: NsUid, code: i32, value: i64 },// SI_QUEUE
       MessageQueue{ sender: TaskKey, ruid: NsUid, value: i64 },           // SI_MESGQ
       Poll        { fd: Fd, band: LinuxPollBand },                        // SI_SIGIO
       ChildExit   { child: TaskKey, code: i32, status: i32 },             // SI_CHLD
       Kernel,                                                             // timers, faults
   }
   pub enum SignalDeliveryOutcome { Delivered(NonZeroUsize), DroppedProtectedInit, Denied, Missing, Exhausted }

   impl Kernel {
       pub fn deliver_signal(&self, caller: &KernelContext, dest: SignalDestination,
                             signal: Option<LinuxSignal>, origin: SignalOrigin)
                             -> SignalDeliveryOutcome;
   }

   deliver_signal resolves dest -> Vec<TaskKey>/(TaskKey,ThreadKey) exactly as
   hvpatch_group_signal/hvpatch_specific_{process,thread}_signal already do, calls the
   existing authorize_signal_target_exact for each, mints the siginfo from `origin`
   (si_pid = sender.id.raw(), NEVER a host pid and never through host_to_ns_or_self),
   charges RLIMIT_SIGPENDING ONCE against the sender's uid across all destinations, and
   posts through post_signal_to_authorized_target. signum 0 resolves and authorizes but
   posts nothing. The zombie rule (hvpatch_signal_observes_zombie) moves inside, so kill
   and pidfd_send_signal cannot diverge again.

   Callers collapse to one line each:
     kill/tkill/tgkill/rt_sigqueueinfo/rt_tgsigqueueinfo (signal.rs), pidfd_send_signal
     (proc.rs:4204), send_async_owner_signal (fs.rs:4753), deliver_notify (mqueue.rs:927).

2. THE PROCESS-DIRECTED SINK BECOMES PER-TASK. Delete PROC_PENDING, SENDER_PID,
   publish_process_signal, take_process_pending, has_process_pending, clear_proc_pending,
   record_sender, last_sender_for. task.shared().pending_signals() and
   thread.signal_state().pending() already exist and already carry the payload; make
   deliver_pending_signal (vcpu_loop/signal.rs:384) read ONLY
   dispatcher.take_deliverable_pending_from(context, tid) and drop the host-slot arm and
   its last_sender_for fallback (:497). Same for rt_sigtimedwait_deliver (signal.rs:2421).

3. HOST-ORIGINATED SIGNALS ROUTE BY ORIGIN, NOT BY PID. A real host signal (tty SIGINT/
   SIGQUIT/SIGTSTP, itimer/POSIX-timer expiry) is genuine host I/O and must keep arriving,
   but the host handler cannot know which Linux process owns it and cannot take the
   registry lock. Two phases:
     // async-signal-safe, lock-free, fixed-size
     pub fn enqueue_host_origin(origin: HostSignalOrigin, signal: LinuxSignal);
     pub enum HostSignalOrigin { ControllingTerminal, Itimer(TaskKey, Which), PosixTimer(TaskKey, PosixTimerId), CarrierFault }
     // dispatch context
     impl Kernel { pub fn drain_host_origins(&self) -> RoutedCount; }
   ControllingTerminal routes to the session's FOREGROUND ProcessGroupId (the kernel
   already tracks session/process_group). Timers already know their owning TaskKey at arm
   time — itimer.rs:26 and posix_timer.rs:28 just have to carry it into the closure instead
   of dropping it. This also fixes setitimer/timer_create cross-process misdelivery for free.

4. mq_notify KEYS ON TaskKey. mqueue.rs:766 uses cx.kernel.task().key(); the registrant is
   held in the kernel's mqueue object (generation-bound), and the backing FILE keeps only
   message bytes + the immutable creator uid. mq_clear_notify compares TaskKey, so B cannot
   unregister A. deliver_notify calls Kernel::deliver_signal(dest: Exact(registrant),
   origin: MessageQueue{..}). SIGEV_THREAD resolves netlink_fd in the REGISTRANT's file
   table via the kernel-graph fd table, not `this`.

5. fasync/dnotify OWNER BECOMES TYPED. OpenDescription stores
   `enum FasyncOwner { Pid(TaskId), Tid(TaskId, LinuxTid), Pgrp(ProcessGroupId) }` set from
   the guest's F_SETOWN value directly (it is already guest-domain), and
   send_async_owner_signal maps it 1:1 to SignalDestination with
   SignalOrigin::Poll { fd, band }. No self_ns_pid(), no ns_to_host_*, no
   queue_self_sigpoll special case — self is just Process(my TaskId), which
   deliver_signal handles because post_signal_to_authorized_target works on self.

6. /proc/self RESOLVES FROM THE CALLER'S TASK. vfs/proc.rs:1836 returns the active
   context's task id (dispatch::resources::with_active_context, the same source
   abi_args.rs:54 caller_task_pid already uses), not self_ns_pid(). Delete
   PidfdTarget::Host and the proc_pid_dir_host_pid pidfd fallback so a pidfd cannot
   name anything but a TaskKey.

7. RETIRE THE PID-NAMESPACE TRANSLATION LAYER IN THE SIGNAL PATH. Under HVPatch the kernel
   graph IS the namespace: root task id == 1 (hvpatch/mod.rs:1022), children 2,3,4...
   namespace::pid::{enabled, ns_to_host_or_self, ns_to_host_pgid, self_ns_pid,
   should_drop_signal_to_init, set_init_handler, NS_INIT_PID} are a second, carrier-scoped
   answer to the same question and must not appear in dispatch/signal.rs, dispatch/fs.rs
   fasync, dispatch/mqueue.rs, or vcpu_loop/signal.rs. Init protection already lives
   correctly at kernel/operations.rs:1135.

8. MAKE IT MECHANICAL. Add `carrier_pid()` as the single named escape, then extend
   .semgrep/typed-domains.yml: std::process::id, libc::{getpid,getppid,getpgrp,getsid,kill,
   killpg,raise}, and namespace::pid::self_ns_pid are ERRORS under crates/carrick-runtime/
   src/{dispatch,vfs,namespace}/ unless the enclosing fn is `#[carrier_scoped]`. Ship it as
   a monotonic baseline (fail on any new finding AND on any baseline entry that stops
   matching) so the file can only shrink. This is item 2/3 of the
   docs/host-facility-boundary.md "make it mechanical" plan, applied to the group that
   actually has live bugs.
audits.risk:
WHAT CAN HANG.

1. Lost wakeup when PROC_PENDING dies. Today the carrier-global mask is a catch-all: a
   signal published from a host handler is found by ANY thread's next delivery cycle, which
   is why misdelivery reads as "it worked". Per-task queues remove that accidental
   redundancy, so a publish that misses its task's wake wedges that task forever in
   pause()/sigsuspend()/futex. Two mitigations, both already proven in this tree: (a) the
   host-origin inbox must be RING-AUTHORITATIVE, scanned rather than gated on a losable
   dirty flag — xsig.rs:246-263 records that gating on XSIG_DIRTY produced the Linux/KVM
   do_sys_poll wedge; (b) post_signal_to_authorized_target already ends in task.wake() +
   parent.wake() after dropping the generation lock, so keep that publish-then-wake order
   and never wake inside lock_signal_generation. A reviewer catches this by running
   ltp sigsuspend/pause/sigwait cases and CPython test_sigwait_thread, and by checking that
   every new publish site is followed by a wake on the same TaskKey.

2. Lock inversion / self-deadlock. Kernel::deliver_signal takes registry.state.read() to
   resolve, then lock_signal_generation per target. Called from fs.rs's fasync path it now
   runs INSIDE a write path that may hold the fd/description lock, and from mqueue inside
   MqLock. A reviewer must confirm deliver_signal never re-enters the fd table or the
   mqueue lock (it must not: origin carries only plain data, and SIGEV_THREAD's fd
   resolution has to happen in a second, lock-free phase). docs/identity-and-scope-domains.md
   item 5 records that an alias-cleanup path re-entering a non-reentrant topology lock
   turned an intended ENOMEM into an unkillable hang.

3. Group fan-out under a lock. hvpatch_group_signal already collects TaskKeys, releases the
   registry lock, then posts. deliver_signal must keep that two-phase shape; posting while
   holding registry.state.read() while post_signal_to_authorized_target calls task.wake()
   is the same inversion.

4. Timer regression. Moving itimer/POSIX-timer delivery from publish_process_signal to an
   owning TaskKey means a timer whose owner exited must drop rather than route, or a fired
   timer spins. The kernel's weak-ref ticket gives this for free, but the FIRING THREAD is
   a plain std::thread with no KernelContext — it must hold a TaskKey (weak), not a
   TaskId. A reviewer checks that setitimer across fork/exec does not leave an orphan
   thread posting into a reused id.

5. Regression surface a fix must not break. The tests protecting the current shape are
   real and were written against the retired model: signal.rs:3625
   ring_drain_publishes_process_directed_signal_visible_to_non_drainer, :3777
   ring_drain_routes_thread_directed_to_target_tid_only, :3928
   ring_drain_discards_thread_directed_for_exited_tid, :3142
   cross_process_sigqueue_usr1_ring_full_returns_eagain_without_host_kill_fallback, and
   :2928 cross_process_xsig_policy_routes_unhostable_signals all exercise the xsig ring and
   must be DELETED with it, not adapted — they encode "one guest process == one host
   process". A reviewer should be suspicious of any patch that keeps them green.

6. Measurement hygiene. Deleting the per-delivery xsig ring scan (dispatch/signal.rs:733,
   mqueue.rs:984) is a small win on a very hot path; do not report it without an ABBA on a
   quiet box, and note that the conformance gate currently running makes any number taken
   today a hypothesis, not a measurement.
audits.test_shape:
RED-FIRST, TWO LIVE GUEST PROCESSES. Every case below is correct today when one Linux
process exists and wrong the instant a second appears — which is exactly why the smoke
lane cannot see them. Each probe prints one deterministic line per event so the Docker
oracle diff is line-exact, and each must be shown FAILING against the current signed
binary before the fix.

1. conformance-probes/src/bin/xprocsigio.rs  (closes fs.rs:4767/4774/4787)
   Parent: pipe(); fcntl(rd, F_SETOWN, getpid()); fcntl(rd, F_SETFL, O_ASYNC);
   sigaction(SIGIO, SA_SIGINFO) recording si_pid/si_code/si_fd; fork(); parent pause().
   Child: write(wr, "x", 1); then _exit(0).
   Expect: exactly "PARENT SIGIO code=POLL_IN fd=<rd> pid=<parent getpid()>" and
   "CHILD no-sigio". Today the parent hangs to the suite deadline (SIGIO dropped by the
   ns_to_host_or_self miss) — a 300.3s "slow" row that is really a hang, per the
   timeout-budget rule.
   Second arm: F_SETOWN(-getpgid(0)) with the parent AND a second child both in the group;
   both must receive it.
   Third arm: F_SETOWN(1) from a child — must reach init, not the writer (proves the
   self_ns_pid()==1 mis-fire).

2. conformance-probes/src/bin/mqnotifyxproc.rs  (closes mqueue.rs:766/941/957/965)
   Parent: mq_open(O_CREAT|O_RDWR); mq_notify(SIGEV_SIGNAL, SIGUSR1, sival_int=0xC0DE);
   sigaction(SIGUSR1, SA_SIGINFO); fork(); pause().
   Child: mq_send("m").
   Expect: "PARENT MESGQ code=SI_MESGQ val=0xc0de" and "CHILD no-usr1". Today the child
   receives SIGUSR1 (or a third process does) and the parent hangs.
   Second arm, the unregister leak: child calls mq_notify(mqd, NULL) BEFORE sending; it
   must return 0 having removed NOTHING, and the parent's notification must still fire.
   Today the child clears the parent's registration because both stamp the carrier pid.
   Third arm, SIGEV_THREAD: parent registers via glibc's SIGEV_THREAD; child sends; the
   payload must land on the parent's netlink fd, not on whatever occupies that fd number
   in the child.

3. conformance-probes/src/bin/procselfpidfd.rs  (closes vfs/proc.rs:1836)
   Child (a forked grandchild of init): fd = open("/proc/self", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY);
   pidfd_send_signal(fd, SIGUSR1, NULL, 0) with a SIGUSR1 handler installed.
   Expect: the CHILD's handler runs, si_pid == child getpid(); init still alive; parent
   still alive. Today /proc/self resolves to guest pid 1 and this signals the container
   init — on the run-elf lane it self-raises into the carrier-global slot and lands on an
   arbitrary process. Add waitid(P_PIDFD, fd) to prove the same fd does not name init.

4. Extend conformance-probes/src/bin/siginfo.rs  (closes SENDER_PID / last_sender_for)
   For each of kill, tgkill, rt_sigqueueinfo, rt_tgsigqueueinfo and pidfd_send_signal sent
   from a SIBLING guest process, assert si_pid == sibling's getpid() and si_uid == its
   real uid, and that si_code is SI_USER / SI_TKILL / SI_QUEUE respectively. Then
   sigwaitinfo() a tty SIGINT and a timer SIGALRM and assert si_pid == 0 (kernel-generated),
   not 1 and not the macOS carrier pid. Today the host-slot fallback yields
   si_pid=1 (pid-ns on) or si_pid=<macOS pid> and si_uid=0.

5. conformance-probes/src/bin/timerowner.rs  (closes PROC_PENDING)
   Parent forks a child that busy-loops in a tight syscall loop; parent arms
   setitimer(ITIMER_REAL, 200ms) with a SIGALRM handler; both print every SIGALRM they
   receive with getpid(). Expect: only the parent ever prints. Today the child steals a
   measurable fraction of the expiries because take_pending_for falls through to the shared
   mask — run 50 expiries so the steal is not a coin flip. Same shape with
   timer_create(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, SIGEV_SIGNAL).

6. Unit-level, in signal.rs / operations.rs
   - zombie parity: pidfd_send_signal to an exited-unreaped child returns 0, matching
     hvpatch_signal_observes_zombie.
   - RLIMIT_SIGPENDING: with RLIMIT_SIGPENDING={0,0} in the SENDER and a blocked SIGRTMIN

   - a compile-time gate rather than a test: the semgrep rule in section 8 of the design,
     with a baseline that fails when an entry stops matching, so removing a site forces
     deleting its baseline line and the file can only shrink.

batches.rationale:
MUST LAND ALONE. `crates/carrick-runtime/src/kernel/objects.rs` is the single most contended file in the campaign: four of the five audits need a new field on `Task`, `Zombie` or `Session`, and every one of those additions lands in the SAME hunk (the struct field list), so they cannot merge in parallel worktrees. This batch is the only place `Task` gains fields for the whole campaign.

What it adds, all verified as absent at HEAD (575c9288d):
(1) `LinuxResource` ordinal enum in carrick-abi replacing the hand-numbered `LINUX_RLIMIT_*` consts, with `from_guest_arg(u64) -> Result<Self, LinuxErrno>` as the ONLY constructor from a guest register, plus `index()`. This names the six resources the ABI has no constant for (Rss, Locks, Msgqueue, Nice, Rtprio, Rttime) and makes `resource as usize` indexing (dispatch/time.rs:963) unrepresentable.
(2) `Task::rlimits: ArcSwap<RlimitSet>` + `rlimit_write: Mutex<()>` + `Task::rlimit(r)` (lock-free `ArcSwap::load`), `replace_rlimit(r, decide)` (read-modify-write returning the PREVIOUS value so prlimit64's report-old-then-apply-new is one critical section), and `RlimitSet::carrick_defaults()` as THE single default table. Copies the `process_credentials: ArcSwap<Credentials>` shape already on `Task` (objects.rs:2331).
(3) `Kernel::process_identity(TaskId) -> Option<ProcessIdentity{pid,parent,process_group,session,state:Live|Zombie}}` implemented as `state.tasks` then `state.zombies`. `Zombie` (objects.rs:4146) ALREADY carries `process_group` and `session`, so this is a lookup, not new state. Three batches consume it.
(4) `Kernel::process_group_exists(ProcessGroupId)` returning true if the group record exists OR any zombie carries that group. The zombie clause is load-bearing: `remove_group_member` (operations.rs:3020) destroys the record when the last LIVE member exits, so a naive probe turns a legitimate reap of the group's last zombie into ESRCH.
(5) `Kernel::rlimit_target(NsPid) -> RlimitTarget{Live{task,key,credentials}|Zombie|Missing}`, resolving a TID to its thread group as Linux does, reusing `live_keys_for_thread`.
(6) `Zombie.uid: NsUid` (the child's REAL uid — `Zombie` carries only `euid` today) and `Task/Zombie.exit_signal: Option<Signal>` seeded from `ClonePlan`, which already carries `fork_parent` so it is the same seam.
(7) `Session` (objects.rs:4101) gains `controlling_tty: Option<TtyId>` and `foreground: Option<ProcessGroupId>`; `TtyId` is a new typed id minted from the open-file description, never a bare fd number.
(8) `Task` nsproxy holding `Arc<NetNs>` / `Arc<UtsNs>`, with `net_ns()/uts_ns()/unshare_*()` mirroring the existing `user_ns()/unshare_user_ns()/inherit_creds_ns_from()` trio (objects.rs:2563-2605) exactly. The `NetNs`/`UtsNs` objects themselves go in the two new files.

(10) `Authority { Guest, Host, Hybrid }` on `Syscall`, plus the `just lint-domains` rules and a FULL monotonic baseline (see sequencing_rationale for why the baseline lands first, not last).

Deliberately NOT here: any file under dispatch/ or vfs/. That is what lets batches 2 and 3 run in parallel immediately after.

batches.name: rlimits-as-task-state
batches.rationale:
RANKED FIRST AMONG THE FIXES ON EVIDENCE, and `docs/host-facility-boundary.md` independently ranks it first. It is the only batch whose defect is already recorded as a failing conformance row: `docs/conformance-closure-ledger.md:3024-3026` carries `go:TestPrlimitFileLimit#1/#2/#3` as carrick `fail` / Docker `ok`, plus `ltp-setrlimit01:2#1` at :4046 — I verified all four rows in the ledger, which is generated from a complete closure run at HEAD 3ef2bf7a with a recorded signed binary digest.

THE DEFECT, verified: `prlimit64` (dispatch/time.rs:868-975) uses its `pid` argument ONLY for an existence probe (`std::process::id()` self-test at :873, `libc::kill(pid,0)` fallback at :880). Every read (:899) and write (:947, :963) goes to `this.proc.lock().rlimit_overrides` — the CALLER's dispatcher-private `ProcState` (dispatch/proc.rs:674). So `prlimit64(child, RLIMIT_NOFILE, {42,max})` returns success, leaves the child at 43, and silently drops the PARENT from 43 to 42, where Linux leaves the parent alone. batches.rationale:
ALONE — it owns proc.rs, fs.rs, vfs/proc.rs and net.rs simultaneously, which is every remaining contended file.

THE LINCHPIN, and it is one function. `namespace::pid::self_ns_pid()` (namespace/pid.rs:352) starts from `std::process::id()`, and under HVPatch the pid-ns region has exactly ONE registered member — `threaded_loop.rs:226` registers the carrier and the HVPatch fork path (vcpu_loop/quiesce.rs:1786+) never calls `register_child` because there is no host process to register. So `self_ns_pid()` is a CONSTANT (1 on the container lane, the raw carrier pid on run-elf) for every logical Linux process, while `enabled()` stays true so 20+ `if enabled()` branches take the arm written for the retired model. That is not an approximate answer; it is a constant function standing where a per-process one belongs.

EVERY DEFECT BELOW IS DOWNSTREAM OF IT:
- `NsPid::names_self()` (abi_args.rs:102) is TRUE for pid 1 from EVERY process. So a guest child calling `capset(hdr{pid:1})` (creds.rs:508) modifies ITSELF instead of returning EPERM; `capget(hdr{pid:1})` returns the child's caps; `getpriority(PRIO_PROCESS,1)` returns the child's nice; `tkill(1,sig)` becomes a self-signal so a child's `kill init` terminates the child; `sched_getparam(1)`/`sched_setaffinity(1)` silently operate on the caller. The narrowed bootstrap-alias arm at abi_args.rs:99 was added precisely to stop this and this arm reinstates it.
- `readlink("/proc/self")` returns "1" for EVERY guest process (vfs/proc.rs:2506); `/proc/thread-self` returns "1/task/1" (:1388). A guest resolving its own pid this way — a common libc/Go/Python idiom — believes it is init.
- `proc_self_magic_link` (fs.rs:1134) treats `/proc/<n>/exe|cwd|root` as self iff n is the carrier pid or 1, so from guest 3 `readlink("/proc/3/exe")` is ENOENT (its own exe unreachable by its own pid) while `readlink("/proc/1/exe")` returns process 3's OWN executable — the exact identity leak the doc comment at :1128 says it exists to prevent. Same for `/proc/1/fdinfo/N` (:1186).
- `get_robust_list(getpid(), …)` returns EPERM reading its own list (proc.rs:1985: `self_pid = std::process::id()`, so the self-test fails and the peer branch runs).
- `PTRACE_TRACEME` registers `libc::getppid()` — the CARRIER's Darwin parent — as the tracer (proc.rs:2745). This is REACHED on HVPatch: `select_ptrace_transport` (proc.rs:412) returns `VirtualHvpatch` and `route_ptrace_request` maps request 0 to `VirtualTraceme`. `ProcessContext::parent_pid()` (hvpatch/mod.rs:352) is one line away.
- SIGIO/SIGURG is SILENTLY DROPPED (fs.rs:4767/4774/4787): the owner test compares a guest pid against `self_ns_pid()`, `ns_to_host_or_self` misses, and the send reaches `bootstrap_signal_send_as` where `host_signal_transport_allowed` is false → ESRCH, discarded by `let _ =`. A parent that does `F_SETOWN(fd,getpid()); O_ASYNC; pause()` hangs FOREVER when the child writes. dnotify has the same shape at :4858 and stamps every registration's owner as init.
- `/proc/<peer-thread-tid>/stat` falls through to `current_thread_states()` (vfs/proc.rs:3560), a PROCESS-GLOBAL (i.e. carrier-wide) registry, and renders PPid/Tgid/pgrp/session as five-digit macOS values. `/proc/<pid>/task/` (vfs/proc.rs:1707) lists the union of EVERY guest process's threads, so a guest counting its own threads over-counts by the whole carrier.
- Netlink autobind (net.rs:5547, and :2509) hands every socket `std::process::id()`, so `getsockname(nl).nl_pid != getpid()` (Linux guarantees the first autobound socket gets portid == pid, which iproute2's rtnl_open and libnl's NL_OWN_PORT both read back) and two guest processes receive the SAME portid where Linux detects the collision.

UTS RIDES ALONG because it lives in the same files and is the same defect class. `ProcState.guest_hostname` (proc.rs:630) is a per-dispatcher String copied by `ProcState::fork_clone` (proc.rs:846) into every fork child — FORK-COPY semantics where Linux has SHARED-NAMESPACE semantics. The mirror-image defect sits on the same object: `network: Arc<RuntimeNetwork>` is Arc-cloned at fork, so NET is carrier-global and can never diverge while UTS is per-process and can never be shared. Both wrong, opposite directions, one reason: neither namespace was an object in the graph. This batch moves the nodename onto `UtsNs` (batch 1's slot) and makes `sethostname` consult `has_effective_capability(CAP_SYS_ADMIN)` — the helper already used three lines away at proc.rs:1929 — instead of returning unconditional EPERM (proc.rs:2852), so a `--privileged` guest that was told `unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS)` succeeded (proc.rs:1912-1936 accepts-and-ignores it) can actually set a name in it.

DELETIONS IN THE SAME CHANGE, per no-backward-compatibility: `self_ns_pid`, `self_ns_ppid`, `ns_to_host_or_self`, `ns_to_host_pgid`, `host_to_ns_or_self`, `host_to_ns_pgid`, `ns_pid_is_session_leader`, and `NsPid::to_host`/`HostPid::to_guest` (abi_args.rs:113-137) — there is no host-pid domain for a guest process any more, so their call sites BECOME COMPILE ERRORS, which is the mechanical forcing function `docs/identity-and-scope-domains.md` asks for. `guest_pid_is_live` becomes `-> bool` and its three `libc::kill(pid,0)` fallbacks (proc.rs:1996, proc.rs:2731, time.rs:880) go. What SURVIVES from namespace/pid.rs is the pid-1 signal policy (`is_default_lethal`, `should_drop_signal_to_init`) re-keyed on `TaskId(1)`.

Note sysv.rs:1544-1549 already REFUSES `self_ns_pid()` for `msg_lspid` and threads `identity_pid()` in instead: the crate already knows the difference.

batches.name: signal-delivery-unification
batches.rationale:
ALONE, and it must FOLLOW batch 4 because batch 4 fixes the OWNER identity (`self_ns_pid` in the fasync path, `/proc/self` in the pidfd path) while this batch fixes the DELIVERY. Splitting them the other way round would leave a correct owner routed through a broken transport.

GOAL: exactly one way to deliver a Linux signal, taking a kernel-graph destination plus an origin carrying the sender's guest identity. `Kernel::deliver_signal(caller, SignalDestination{Process|Thread|ProcessGroup|CallerGroup|Broadcast|Exact}, signal, SignalOrigin{Kill|Tkill|Queued|MessageQueue|Poll|ChildExit|Kernel})`. The model already exists and is CORRECT — `hvpatch_group_signal` (signal.rs:1160) resolves kill(0)/kill(-pgid)/kill(-1) entirely from the ProcessGroupId table with the i32::MIN checked_neg fix, Linux's success/ESRCH/EPERM aggregation, init excluded from broadcast and si_pid stamped from the caller's TaskKey; and `post_signal_to_authorized_target` (operations.rs:1382) is generation-bound so an exit/reap/id-reuse race can only make a post FAIL, never redirect to the new occupant of a reused number. Everything else must be lowered onto them.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG (verified globals at carrick-signal-core/src/lib.rs:90 and :418):
- `static PROC_PENDING: AtomicU64` is ONE carrier-global process-directed pending bitmask. `vcpu_loop/signal.rs:384` calls `take_pending_for(tid)` for every thread of every guest process and on a per-tid miss drains this shared mask. I confirmed the publishers: itimer expiry (carrick-vmm-hvf/src/timer_delivery.rs:92), POSIX-timer expiry (posix_timer.rs:28), tty SIGINT (vcpu_kick.rs:500/628/668/683), the signal-pump handler (carrick-hal/src/signal_pump.rs:198), and `raise_for_self`. So process A's `setitimer(ITIMER_REAL,1s)` can be received by process B, which dies with exit 142 while A's alarm never fires. Wrong in units of "which Linux process", silently, with no errno.
- `static SENDER_PID: [AtomicI32; 64]` is a carrier-global 64-slot array of HOST pids used to synthesise si_pid, consumed at vcpu_loop/signal.rs:497 and signal.rs:2421, and then passed through `host_to_ns_or_self` → 1, plus `cred_ipc::read_target` → None (because `bind_hvpatch_process` calls `cred_ipc::unpublish()`, mod.rs:3266) so si_uid is forced to 0. A guest SA_SIGINFO handler or `sigwaitinfo()` observes `si_pid = 1` or the macOS carrier pid, and `si_uid = 0`. That is the SCM_CREDENTIALS defect shape from the doctrine recurring in the signal path — and two guest processes overwrite each other's slot for the same signum.
- mq_notify stamps the registrant as `std::process::id()` (mqueue.rs:766) into the queue's BACKING FILE header, so the wrong domain is DURABLE: guest B's `mq_notify(mqd, NULL)` silently unregisters guest A's notification, and because the stamp always equals the carrier pid the `pid == std::process::id()` branch at :941 is ALWAYS taken, queueing A's SIGEV_SIGNAL notification into the SENDER's pending set. A registers and blocks; B sends; B dies of SIGUSR1 and A never wakes.
- ONE BUG IS MASKING ANOTHER, and this dictates that identity and delivery move in a SINGLE change: `libc::kill(pid, host_signo)` at mqueue.rs:957 is the only `libc::kill` in a guest-authority dispatch path NOT behind `hvpatch_lane_active()`. It is unreachable only because :941 always matches. The moment :766/:941 are corrected to `identity_pid()`, it fires with a GUEST TaskId — and since `root_bootstrap_identity` seeds ids at 1, that is `kill(1, …)` to macOS launchd. signal.rs:2744-2749 predicted exactly this as a prerequisite; the seed change landed and this site was not covered.
- `pidfd_send_signal` returns ESRCH for a zombie (proc.rs:4214) where `kill(2)` was already fixed to keep a zombie addressable (b9292468d, `hvpatch_signal_observes_zombie`). Same divergence, two code paths, one already has the right helper — so the zombie rule moves INSIDE `deliver_signal` and they cannot diverge again.
- RLIMIT_SIGPENDING is charged only in `hvpatch_specific_thread_signal` (signal.rs:1348) and `sigqueueinfo_common` (:2248), not in the process or group paths, and `pending_signal_count` (:2093) counts the CALLER's task — so a cross-process RT send is bounded by the SENDER's queue depth. So under `--network bridge`, `ioctl(SIOCGIFADDR,"eth0")` returns the MAC's en0 IPv4 (192.168.1.42) while the rtnetlink dump for the SAME interface returns the container address (172.x). Two more hardcodes on the same path: SIOCGIFNETMASK returns 255.255.255.255 (fs.rs:8719) where both the model and getifaddrs carry a real prefix, and SIOCGIFMTU returns 1500 (fs.rs:8728) including for `lo`, where Linux reports 65536.

THE IFINDEX SPACE IS DEFINED IN ONE PLACE AND CONSUMED FROM ANOTHER. `linux_if_nametoindex` (fs.rs:1300) is a hardcoded `match { "lo" => 1, "eth0" => 2, _ => None }` backing SIOCGIFINDEX (fs.rs:8601) and SIOCGIFNAME (fs.rs:8577), while `LinuxNetworkModel::from_spec` (network/model.rs:88) names uplinks `eth{idx}` at index idx+2. /proc/net DISAGREES WITH RTNETLINK. `synthetic_proc_net_route` in host mode (vfs/proc.rs:1551) emits ONE row — eth0 default, gateway 0.0.0.0, no loopback route — while RTM_GETROUTE (support.rs:1163-1188) synthesizes one connected route per address INCLUDING 127.0.0.0/8. Two guest-facing renderings of one table that disagree on row count. `host_mc_interfaces()` (vfs/proc.rs:1627) is a FOURTH uplink rule whose whole purpose is to produce a `has_ipv6` boolean — and `synthetic_proc_net_if_inet6` (vfs/proc.rs:1504) then has to INVENT `fe800000000000000000000000000001` to print, which is why the fe80:: fabrication was expressible at all. `/proc/net/if_inet6` cannot be correct while its input carries no addresses; batch 3 replaced the bool with real addresses, and this batch makes the renderer read them and DELETES the template.

Each earlier batch deletes the path it replaced, in its own commit, per no-backward-compatibility. What is left here is the residue that could not be deleted earlier because it had consumers in more than one batch:
